description: EF Core complex property indexing extensions for EF Core 10.
releaseNotes:
The last 5.x minor with a change of its own: the line refuses EF Core 11, whose successor is CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit.

Changed answers

- Registration: on SQL Server and PostgreSQL, the core differ refuses a complex index carrying that provider's index options and names UseSqlServerComplexIndexes() or UseNpgsqlComplexIndexes(). With UseComplexIndexes(), EnsureCreated() created the index without its property-level options (#92 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/92), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#the-core-differ-refuses-sql-server-and-postgresql-index-options)).
- Registration: on PostgreSQL, the core differ also refuses exclusion constraints, temporal constraints and temporal foreign keys, and on SQL Server a unique complex index over nullable columns. With UseComplexIndexes(), EnsureCreated() created the tables without those constraints and the index without its IS NOT NULL filter (#150 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/150), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#the-core-differ-refuses-the-satellites-constraints-and-null-filter)).
- Indexes: a complex index declared on a TPC type is created on the table of every type derived from it, as EF Core's own indexes are. On a concrete base it was created on the base's table only, so a unique index admitted duplicates among the derived types' rows (#93 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/93), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Indexes: a complex index with DbOrder.NullsFirst/NullsLast ordering or an expression part fails at migrations add on SQLite and other providers without a satellite, and under the core differ on SQL Server and PostgreSQL. Where SQLite accepts double-quoted strings, it applied with a constant column in place of its ordering or expression (#134 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/134), #172 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/172), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#nulls-ordering-and-expression-parts-fail-on-sqlite)).
- Indexes: on PostgreSQL and SQL Server, an IncludeProperties(…) entry that names neither a property nor a column of the table fails at migrations add. When its property was removed, the migration dropped only the column: PostgreSQL dropped the index with it and applied cleanly, SQL Server failed at apply (#142 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/142), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#include-entries-must-name-a-column)).
- Migrations: on SQLite without UseComplexIndexes(), migrations add refuses a migration that rebuilds a table with a complex index, naming the indexes and the ways out. It scaffolded a migration that applied cleanly and dropped every complex index on the table (#86 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/86), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#sqlite-refuses-a-table-rebuild-that-would-drop-complex-indexes)).
- Migrations: on SQLite with UseComplexIndexes() after UseSqlite(), a migration that rebuilds a table drops its complex indexes before the rebuild and creates them after it. Applied without that registration, the migration fails before the rebuild (#95 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/95), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#sqlite-re-creates-complex-indexes-after-a-table-rebuild)).

Breaking

- Registration: UseComplexIndexes(), AddComplexIndexes() and the design-time registration dotnet ef runs throw InvalidOperationException on an EF Core major other than 10, naming CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit for EF Core 11. EF Core 10 on .NET 11 keeps working (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#ef-core-11-is-refused-at-registration)).
- Indexes: on a provider without a satellite whose index names keep their case, complex index names that differ only in case fail at migrations add; rename one (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#rename-complex-index-names-that-differ-only-in-case)).
- Indexes: a complex index on a TPC type with derived types fails at migrations add when it reads a member of a complex property, which EF Core 10 maps to no column in a derived table; map the member as a regular property (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).

Added

- CustomMigrationsModelDiffer.RequiresIndexRecreation, a protected hook through which a provider's differ drops an unchanged complex index before a base operation that cannot run while it exists, and creates it after.
- CustomMigrationsModelDiffer.ImplicitFilter, a protected hook through which a provider's differ gives an index declared without a filter the one its EF Core convention would give it.
- CustomMigrationsModelDiffer.IndexNameComparer, a protected hook through which a provider's differ says how it compares index names: without regard to case by default and on SQL Server, ordinally on PostgreSQL.
- CustomMigrationsModelDiffer(…, ICurrentDbContext), a constructor taking the context the migration is diffed for, and ComplexIndexAnnotations.AfterTableRebuild, the mark on a create that runs after SQLite's table rebuild (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#sqlite-re-creates-complex-indexes-after-a-table-rebuild)).

Changed

- Indexes: a complex index declared on the abstract base of a TPC hierarchy is created on every concrete table, as EF Core's own indexes are, where it failed at migrations add (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Indexes: on SQLite, an explicit name on a complex index of a TPC type stays on that type's table, and each derived table's copy takes the name followed by its table. A copy's name past the identifier limit is shortened as EF Core's are (#145 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/145), #167 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/167), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Packaging: each package carries the version's section of its changelog as its NuGet release notes, which nuget.org's Release Notes tab and Visual Studio's Updates tab show.
- Packaging: the release notes, the README on nuget.org and the GitHub release link the documentation at the version's tag, so they keep describing the version they shipped with after main moves on to the next line.
- Packaging: the PostgreSQL and SQL Server packages depend on exactly their own version of EFCore.ComplexIndexes, and the core differ refuses a satellite of another version, naming both. Update the packages together: a 5.4.x satellite beside core 5.5.0 was refused as the core differ (#169 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/169)).

Fixed

- Indexes: on SQLite, complex index names that differ only in case, from each other or from a native index, fail at migrations add, where they failed at apply because SQLite compares them without regard to case (Index names (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/README.md#single-column-index-on-a-complex-property)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/src/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/CHANGELOG.md
